concerns.text: The plan relies on a standard two‑sided paired t‑test (or Wilcoxon fallback) to assess whether the static index degrades performance. A non‑significant p‑value is interpreted as evidence that the static index ‘does not significantly hurt’ the model, which conflates lack of evidence with evidence of equivalence. To support the research question (“how much dynamic retrieval signal can be compressed without incurring a statistically significant degradation”), the methodology should include an equivalence test or define a practically insignificant effect size margin (e.g., Δlog PPL < δ) and power the study to detect that margin. Without this, the conclusion that dynamic retrieval is unnecessary when p ≥ 0.05 is methodologically unsound.
